subject: Service commitments: proposed exception matrix, credit ladder & patch windows
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@deltacore.com>, Sarah Li <sli@deltacore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service commitments: proposed exception matrix, credit ladder & patch windows

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for walking through the Order Form yesterday. As promised I'm attaching a consolidated draft of the service commitments section (Redwood_Support_Commitment_Draft_v3.docx) and a simple CSV that enumerates our proposed planned patch windows by region (Patch_Window_Table.csv).

High-level asks from DeltaCore we captured during the call:
- Clarify uptime measurement interval and blackout carveouts for scheduled patches
- Define the credit ladder for tiered availability shortfalls (P1/P2 buckets)
- Lock in response-time targets for incident severities and on-call handoffs
- Agree process for emergency maintenance and cross-region failover

What we'd like from you this week:
1) Legal redlines on the MSA/Order Form text for the support section (call out any definition shifts for \"Available\" or \"Downtime\");
2) Ops confirmation that the patch windows in the CSV are acceptable or propose alternatives;
3) Procurement timeline for final signature / DocuSign.

I'll coordinate a short sync with Lauren (legal) and Ben (ops) once we have initial redlines so we can avoid multiple rounds. If you prefer we can prepare a markup that replaces the current credit formula with a step-function ladder (example included in v3).

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Support_Commitment_Draft_v3.docx (draft), Patch_Window_Table.csv (proposed windows).

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@deltacore.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sli@deltacore.com>
Cc: procurement@deltacore.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service commitments: proposed exception matrix, credit ladder & patch windows

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the consolidated draft. Quick read-through notes from our side:

1) Credit model: DeltaCore prefers credits tied to total monthly bill (standard) but we want to avoid open-ended liability for minor blips. Can you provide an example calculation for a 99.5% vs 99.9% outcome under your ladder? The v3 doc references a piecewise approach but we need a worked example.
2) Patch windows: your CSV shows weekly 2-hour windows during local 02:00–04:00. That generally works but can you confirm how you define the start/stop for multi-region rollouts where replicas failover?
3) Response SLAs: we need a clearer policy for initial triage vs full remediation. For P1 incidents we expect a one-hour initial response and a four-hour remediation target for single-region incidents. Are those realistic?

We will circulate to procurement/legal and get back with formal redlines by Friday. If Redwood can include one example calculation in the draft and a short paragraph describing multi-region patch behavior it will speed review.

— Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Cloud Ops, DeltaCore

Folks — forwarding Alex's early feedback from DeltaCore. Short notes / proposed owner map: 

- Ben: please confirm multi-region patch behavior wording and add a short paragraph on \"failover window\" semantics for replicas (DeltaCore wants clarity on start/stop of the patch event across regions). See Patch_Window_Table.csv for the planned windows.
- Aditya: can you produce the example calculations for the credit ladder (99.9% vs 99.5% vs 98.0%) based on a sample monthly bill ($50k) and include a capped maximum credit? DeltaCore explicitly called out avoiding open-ended liability.
- Lauren: please prioritize a legal pass on the Availability definition and the emergency maintenance carveout. They may push to expand what counts as \"Scheduled Maintenance\".

I'll propose a 30-minute sync on Friday with Alex if we have updated text + example calc; otherwise we take redlines and iterate.

Subject: Re: Service commitments: proposed exception matrix, credit ladder & patch windows

Rachel / team — attaching a short legal markup (Legal_Markup_Service_Commitments.pdf) with three principal suggestions:

1) Definitions: tighten \"Available\" to mean \"service endpoints successfully responding to authenticated requests\" and add a performance clause that excludes transient latency spikes < 2 minutes per incident from availability calculations. This prevents microsecond blips from triggering credits.
2) Emergency maintenance carveout: allow for limited immediate maintenance when there is an active security exploit, with a 24-hour post-event notice to the customer and a documented remediation timeline.
3) Credit cap: accept a step-function credit ladder but cap monthly credits at 30% of monthly recurring charges (MRC). We recommend Redwood keeps the cap and an internal approval gate for anything above 30%.

Operational notes for Ben: the legal markup references the patch-window semantics you will provide in the CSV; please verify the phrasing on distributed rollouts (we suggested an overlap approach so an individual region's window is the authoritative start/stop).

Attachment stub: Legal_Markup_Service_Commitments.pdf

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Service commitments: proposed exception matrix, credit ladder & patch windows

Alex / Sarah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've incorporated the items below into a consolidated v4 draft (attached as a link in HubSpot and in the Drive folder). Summary of agreed positions from Redwood:

- Availability definition: we will adopt the tightened wording Lauren proposed and exclude transient latency spikes < 2 minutes from availability calculations.
- Patch windows / multi-region: Ben confirmed an \"authoritative region\" approach in the CSV and added a short paragraph describing overlap behavior for replicas. See Patch_Window_Table.csv.
- Credit ladder & cap: Aditya's worked example is included: for a $50k MRC month, 99.9% => $250 credit, 99.5% => $1500 credit, 98.0% => capped at 30% MRC ($15k). The cap and step-function ladder are included in the draft.
- Emergency maintenance: we accept a narrowly-scoped security carveout with 24-hour post-event notice and a documented remediation timeline.

Next steps:
1) If DeltaCore is comfortable with these positions we will prepare the final Order Form addendum for signature via DocuSign. I can issue the DocuSign packet once procurement confirms the signatory and billing contact.
2) If you have additional legal language to propose, please send a single combined markup back to Lauren by Thursday EOD to avoid another round.
